item.title: Mets’ Jeff Albert Not Returning To Coaching Staff In 2027
item.dc:creator: Anthony Franco
item.description: The Mets announced that director of hitting Jeff Albert and quality assurance coach Danny Barnes will not be on the 2027 coaching staff. Anthony ...
item.content:encoded:
The Mets announced that director of hitting Jeff Albert and quality assurance coach Danny Barnes will not be on the 2027 coaching staff. Anthony DiComo of MLB.com, who first reported the news, suggests it’s possible they’ll find different roles in the organization but are free to pursue other opportunities. DiComo adds that the rest of the staff, aside from batting practice pitcher Kevin Mahoney, is expected to return in Andy Green’s first full season in the manager’s office.

Albert has been in the New York organization since 2022. He spent fours years as their director of hitting, overseeing the team’s offensive program. Albert joined the uniformed coaching staff last offseason with the same title. Troy Snitker was hired as the team’s hitting coach last year, while assistant hitting coach Rafael Fernandez has been in the organization for a couple decades.

The Mets underperformed in most aspects in 2026. That extended to the offense, as they tied for 20th in scoring and were in the bottom third of MLB in all three slash stats. They did pick things up later in the season, but the overall results were a disappointment for a lineup with as much talent as they had.

DiComo writes that the Mets haven’t determined whether they’ll hire a direct replacement in what had been Albert’s role. It’s possible they instead bring on another assistant who’d work underneath Snitker as the lead hitting voice. In either case, they’re opting mostly for continuity on the staff despite the managerial change. Green took over Carlos Mendoza’s staff when the latter was fired in late June. Although he was initially expected to move back to the front office at season’s end, Green accepted the full-time position and signed a three-year extension in September.

item.title: Mets’ Jared Young Expected To Be Ready For 2027 Season
item.dc:creator: Charlie Wright
item.description: Mets first baseman Jared Young had his 2026 campaign cut short after a nasty collision with Nolan McLean. He was knocked unconscious and had ...
item.content:encoded:
Mets first baseman Jared Young had his 2026 campaign cut short after a nasty collision with Nolan McLean. He was knocked unconscious and had to be stretchered off the field. Anthony DiComo of MLB.com spoke to Young yesterday and reports he is recovering well and is expected to be ready for Spring Training.

Young suffered a concussion along with neck and ear issues. He hasn’t fully regained his hearing, but anticipates it will return soon. He can’t remember the hours after the collision.

“How quick baseball can turn into life,” Young said, relayed by DiComo. “It was a scary thing, but it’s real. I cared about getting a hit that morning. I wanted to win that game, and I wanted to hit a home run and celebrate with my teammates. Very quickly did [that change to] I just wanted to get home.”

The unfortunate injury ended a solid season for Young. He slashed .266/.330/.429 across 103 games in his first extended look in the big leagues. Young broke camp with the team but went down in April with a knee injury that required surgery. He returned near the end of May and became an everyday starter at first base and DH.

[Related: Offseason Outlook: New York Mets]

Young stepped into regular reps with Jorge Polanco and Mark Vientos ailing. Polanco was set to be New York’s answer at first base after Pete Alonso departed in free agency. Instead, wrist and ankle injuries limited him to 37 games. Vientos broke his hand shortly before the All-Star Break and didn’t return until the final day of August.

Polanco still has a year left on the $40MM deal he signed over the winter. He’ll be in the mix at first base in 2027. Vientos remains a corner infield option as well. There could be openings around the infield if the club trades Polanco, Marcus Semien, or Francisco Lindor this offseason. Bo Bichette can also opt out of his contract. It seems likely that something will change on this roster, which should afford Young opportunties next season.
